controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 1,783 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of KELT-11 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer IRAC). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of KELT-11's planets in this map from above, to scale, with KELT-11 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

KELT-11 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 25 measured bins from Changeat et al. 2020 (Hubble Space Telescope satellite, Wide Field Camera 3), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors. The archive holds 1 other paper for this planet; this chart draws the one with the most bins.

KELT-11 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (62, 89, 100) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 55092869, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 28-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
